standard.title: Symbols in still and moving images
standard.description: analyse how symbols in still and moving images augment meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students analyse how vectors, angle and social distance in visual texts create perspective (AC9E7LA07). They have not yet examined how symbols within images augment meaning through cultural or conventional associations that extend beyond what is literally depicted.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse how symbols in still and moving images augment meaning, including how symbolic meanings differ across groups and cultures.

nodes.label: Symbols as meaning beyond the literal
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify visual symbols in images and explain the meanings they carry beyond their literal depiction.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one visual symbol in a still or moving image (e.g. a season, colour, weather element) and explain the additional meaning it contributes beyond its literal presence.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how specific seasons, weather and colours function as conventional symbols in a range of still images, films and picture books, evaluating what meanings they contribute to viewer understanding.
wider: Compare how the same visual symbol (e.g. water, fire, white) carries different connotations across cultural contexts, identifying where meanings converge and diverge
Examine how symbols from First Nations Australian art encode cultural knowledge, where the same symbol may have multiple layered meanings or different meanings across different Nations/communities

response_modes.reason: Students default to Western conventional symbolism (white = purity, red = danger) and miss cross-cultural variation. Exposure to diverse cultural contexts — particularly First Nations Australian visual symbolism — reveals that symbolic meaning is culturally constructed, not universal.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The elaborations explicitly foreground First Nations Australian visual symbolism as a rich and substantively different system of meaning-making. This is among the most educationally significant width opportunities in the Y9 Language strand — it connects semiotic analysis to cultural respect and genuinely broadens understanding of how visual symbol systems work.
success_criteria: Student identifies a visual symbol and names a meaning it contributes beyond its literal presence
Student connects the symbolic meaning to a cultural or conventional association that grounds it
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot identify symbols as culturally constructed meanings cannot analyse how the same symbol varies across still versus moving image contexts at N2 — they have no framework for the meaning-augmentation concept.

nodes.label: Symbols augmenting meaning across image types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how symbols augment meaning differently in still versus moving images, explaining how context and sequence affect symbolic interpretation.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse how a symbol in a still image augments meaning, then compare with how the same or similar symbol works in a moving image where sequence and context add further layers.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how symbols augment meaning across both still and moving images, explaining how the temporal dimension of moving images — sequence, juxtaposition, duration — changes how symbols accumulate or transform meaning.
wider: Analyse how a film uses a recurring symbol across its duration, tracing how the symbol's meaning evolves through accumulation and contextual shift
Compare how the same cultural symbol is used in still advertisement images versus moving film contexts, examining how medium shapes symbolic interpretation

response_modes.reason: Analysing symbols across still and moving images requires students to coordinate understanding of static symbolism with the temporal logic of moving images (repetition, transformation, juxtaposition). The integration — how a symbol's meaning is augmented differently by medium — is the analytical target.

success_criteria: Student analyses how a symbol augments meaning in at least one image type (still or moving)
Student explains how the medium (still vs moving) affects how the symbolic meaning is conveyed or accumulated
